Act as release orchestrator for this repository. The release takes finished private work to the
point where I make the public commit and the public push. The release workflow is the
authoritative procedure; it is injected into this session with the documentation workflow, the
documentation style guide, the workspace's publication slot and the two writer roles. A release's
first step merges the integration branch into the plan's branch in this worktree, and a hotfix skips
it because it runs in the integration worktree. Step 2 is the export:
`python AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PUBLISHING/export.py`.

This session runs in the released plan's worktree, or in the integration worktree for a hotfix; the
merge into the integration branch happens in that branch's own worktree, as step 7 says. A hotfix
has no plan: there is no plan's `docs-pass.md` list and no plan to close. Your inputs are the
uncommitted public changes after a fresh export, the open plan's
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/docs-pass.md` list (delete each item once resolved) and this
conversation.

Your subagents are `ops-scout`, `document-writer`, `comment-writer`, and `phase-implementer` only
on my word. Any other subagent requires my explicit permission. Spawn every one in the background.
Ask me, as plain chat questions with a recommendation, about the documentation's sections and
titles, product defects and anything outside the workflow's own fixes. Never edit `AGENTS.md` or
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/` unless I say so, except deleting resolved `docs-pass.md` items and the plan
closure I approve.

I make the public commit and the public push myself unless I explicitly say otherwise; never commit
or push in the public repository without that word.

Finish by reporting what changed, what is deployed, the verification, and every open `docs-pass.md`
item with its reason. Then I check, commit and push.

Release coordination: plan-b merges second, over plan-c. Merge plan-b into main. Keep plan-b open until plan-a's release, which merges last, and hand it every docs-pass item on a shared file, recorded with its owner in docs-pass.md. Clear an item that this branch already resolved and say why. Report the merge and the open items, then stop.

This is a test run of the toy project. No export, public checkout or deployment applies: publish.md is authoritative and the toy publishes nothing, so skip those steps. Merge in the integration worktree and resolve every conflict by the shared designs in AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/ and the plans' done contracts, then run the fast gate and the rendered-image gate in main. The root README and the documentation pages belong to the documentation hotfix after the last release, so leave them out unless a merge breaks a statement in them. Ask me only for product decisions and anything the workflow cannot settle.

# Geometry Plan

> **Status:** scoped forward plan on branch `plan-b`.
> **Scope:** what a hit records and which shapes exist: the front-face flag, texture coordinates,
> planes, triangles and bounding boxes (`docs/requirements.md` items 7 to 10).
> **Out of scope:** materials and scattering (the materials plan); the PNG writer, the command line
> and progress output (the output plan).
> **Target:** a correct, small hobby raytracer.
>
> **How to use this plan:** expand exactly one phase into an implementation-grade phase from
> current code before coding.

## Phase status

| Phase | Title | Status | Gate level | Depends on | Phase file | Exit state | Move-on gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Face side and texture coordinates | done | standard | - | `done/B1-face-side-and-texture-coordinates.md` | every hit records its face side and (u, v) | gates green |
| B2 | Planes and triangles | done | standard | B1 | `done/B2-planes-and-triangles.md` | the scene can hold planes and triangles | gates green, rendered image shows a triangle |
| B3 | Bounding boxes | done | standard | B2 | `done/B3-bounding-boxes.md` | the scene list skips objects whose box the ray misses | gates green, same image as before |
| Z1 | Closing survey and user acceptance | done | minimal | B1 + B2 + B3 | `done/Z1-closing-survey-and-user-acceptance.md` | the user accepts the result | the user accepts |

## How to implement this plan

Read `docs/requirements.md` and the code a phase touches before detailing it. Never invent a name.
Commit whenever useful. Run the fast gate in `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/gates.md`.

## Binding design rules

- `HitRecord` in `src/hittable.rs` stays the one record every shape returns. A helper on it sets
  the normal against the ray and records the face side, so every shape does it the same way.
- One module per shape in `src/`.

## Starting state

`HitRecord` in `src/hittable.rs` holds `t`, `point` and the outward `normal`; `Sphere` in
`src/sphere.rs` builds it. `HittableList` tests every object. `Vec3::cross` exists and is unused.

## Scoped phases

### B1 - Face side and texture coordinates

`HitRecord` gains `front_face` and `u`, `v`. A helper sets the normal against the ray from the
outward normal. `Sphere` fills (u, v) from latitude and longitude. The normal-colouring in
`src/main.rs` keeps working.

### B2 - Planes and triangles

`src/plane.rs` (a point and a normal; (u, v) from the hit position along two in-plane axes, modulo
1) and `src/triangle.rs` (three vertices, Möller-Trumbore; (u, v) barycentric). The scene adds a
triangle.

### B3 - Bounding boxes

**Status:** done. The frozen contract is `done/B3-bounding-boxes.md`.

An `Aabb` type, a `bounding_box` method on `Hittable` returning `Option<Aabb>` (none for a plane),
and `HittableList` testing a box before its object.

### Z1 - Closing survey and user acceptance

**Status:** done. The frozen contract and the carry-overs are in
`done/Z1-closing-survey-and-user-acceptance.md`.

The binding closing survey of everything the plan added or changed: one read-only `ops-scout` per
area in parallel, then one independent `ops-scout` cross-checking every finding against the code, and
the orchestrator writes the dated note in `benchmarks/`. Findings go to the user; none are fixed in
this phase. Also render the scene, compare it with the requirements, and ask the user to accept.

## Carry-overs

The release-merge carry-overs are listed in `done/Z1-closing-survey-and-user-acceptance.md`.

## B2 - Planes and triangles

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** B1 (`done/B1-face-side-and-texture-coordinates.md`): `HitRecord` carries `front_face`,
`u` and `v`, and `HitRecord::new` is the only constructor. The cross-plan shape is settled in

**Gate level:** standard.

**Frozen contract:**
- `src/plane.rs` holds `Plane { pub point: Vec3, pub normal: Vec3 }`, where `normal` is a unit vector
  supplied to `Plane::new(point, normal)`. `Plane::hit` reports no hit when the ray direction is
  perpendicular to the normal or `t` falls outside the exclusive `t_min..t_max` interval. It derives
  (u, v) from the hit point's position along a tangent and bitangent pair of the plane, each wrapped
  with `rem_euclid(1.0)` into `0..1`, and builds its record through the six-argument
  `HitRecord::new` with its outward normal.
- `src/triangle.rs` holds `Triangle { pub a: Vec3, pub b: Vec3, pub c: Vec3 }`, counter-clockwise seen
  from its front face. `Triangle::hit` is Möller-Trumbore: it reports no hit when the determinant is
  below `1e-9` in magnitude, when the barycentric `u` lies outside `0..=1`, when `v < 0` or
  `u + v > 1`, or when `t` falls outside the exclusive interval. Its outward normal is
  `edge1.cross(edge2).unit()` and its (u, v) are the barycentric weights of `b` and `c` relative to
  `a`, passed to `HitRecord::new` unchanged.
- Neither shape carries a material on this branch. Both build records through the six-argument
  `HitRecord::new`. The release merge adds `material: Rc<dyn Material>` to `Plane`, `Triangle` and
  both `new` signatures, and passes it to the seven-argument constructor.

  `(0.5, 0.5, 1.0)` from its `(0, 0, 1)` normal.
- `Vec3::cross` carries no `#[allow(dead_code)]` and no comment, and both shapes call it.
- The rendered 200 by 100 image shows a flat light-blue triangle with straight edges and a horizontal
  base on the right, wholly in the sky above the ground, while the sphere keeps its shaded normal
  colours and every other pixel is unchanged.
- `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/project.md` lists `plane.rs` and `triangle.rs` in the repository map.

**Proof in the tree:** `src/plane.rs` test
`a_ray_through_the_plane_records_the_hit_and_texture_coordinates_that_wrap`, `src/triangle.rs` test
`a_ray_through_the_triangle_hits_its_front_face_with_barycentric_coordinates`, and nine passing tests
in `cargo test`.

## B3 - Bounding boxes

**Status:** done.
**Depends on:** B2 (`done/B2-planes-and-triangles.md`): `Plane` and `Triangle` build their records
through the six-argument `HitRecord::new`, `HittableList::hit` keeps the nearest `HitRecord`, and the
scene holds one triangle.
**Gate level:** standard.

**Frozen contract:**
- `src/aabb.rs` holds `Aabb { pub min: Vec3, pub max: Vec3 }`, `Aabb::new(min, max)` for two opposite
  corners, and `Aabb::hit(&self, ray: &Ray, t_min: f64, t_max: f64) -> bool`, the slab test that
  reports whether the ray crosses the box with some `t` in `t_min..t_max`. A ray component of exactly
  zero is parallel to its slab, and the ray then misses only when its origin lies outside that slab.
  The box is a value derived on each call; no shape stores, caches or refits one.
- `Hittable` in `src/hittable.rs` declares `fn bounding_box(&self) -> Option<Aabb>` with a default
  body returning `None`, the box of an object with no finite extent. `Plane` and `HittableList` take
  the default, so a plane is always tested. Only `Sphere` and `Triangle` override it.
- `Sphere::bounding_box` returns the box from center minus the radius to center plus the radius on
  every axis. `Triangle::bounding_box` returns the corner-wise minimum and maximum of its three
  vertices.
- `HittableList::hit` asks `object.bounding_box()` first and skips the object with `continue` when the
  box's `hit` reports false, using the same `limit` (the nearest hit's `t`, or `t_max`) that the
  object test uses. An object without a box is still tested.
- `src/main.rs` declares `mod aabb;` as the first module. `ray_colour`, `render`, the scene, the
  camera and the writers are unchanged.
- The rendered 200 by 100 image is byte-identical to the B2 image: the flat light-blue triangle on the
  right in the sky, the centred sphere with shaded normal colours, and the green ground.
- `AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/project.md` lists `aabb.rs` in the repository map. `docs/` and
  `README.md` are unchanged, and `docs/requirements.md` item 10 describes the box report, the list
  test and the boxless plane.

**Proof in the tree:** `src/aabb.rs` test
`a_ray_hits_the_box_it_crosses_and_misses_the_box_beside_it`, `src/hittable.rs` test

===== AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/plan-a-A2+plan-b-B2.md
# Shared design: plan-a-A2 + plan-b-B2 (materials × geometry)

Agreed by the plan-a and plan-b orchestrators. Both plans read this as the one copy. It settles
implementation detail only; the one product choice it cannot settle is listed as an open
user-owned decision.

## Target shape of the shared code

`src/hittable.rs` holds one `HitRecord`, not `Copy`:

```rust
pub struct HitRecord {
    pub t: f64,
    pub point: Vec3,
    /// Always faces against the incoming ray (requirement 7).
    pub normal: Vec3,
    pub front_face: bool,
    pub u: f64,
    pub v: f64,
    pub material: Rc<dyn Material>,
}
```

One constructor:

```rust
pub fn new(ray: &Ray, t: f64, point: Vec3, outward_normal: Vec3, u: f64, v: f64, material: Rc<dyn Material>) -> Self
```

It sets `front_face = ray.direction.dot(outward_normal) < 0.0`, then `normal = outward_normal` when
`front_face`, otherwise `-outward_normal`.

`HittableList::hit` reads the nearest distance through a borrow:
`let limit = nearest.as_ref().map_or(t_max, |hit| hit.t);`.

Every shape holds an `Rc<dyn Material>` and passes it to `HitRecord::new`.

Spheres derive `(u, v)` identically on both branches, from the outward normal, so the sphere merge is
textual:

let outward_normal = (point - self.center) / self.radius;

/// Every pixel's colour, row by row from the top, each pixel averaging `samples` jittered rays, with

fn render(width: usize, height: usize, samples: usize) -> Vec<Colour> {

    pixels

# Requirements

A small raytracer with no dependencies beyond the Rust standard library. It renders one fixed scene
and writes the image to a file. Every render is reproducible: the same options give the same bytes.

## Materials

1. Every object has a material. A ray that hits an object scatters by that material and the colour
   is the material's attenuation times the colour the scattered ray sees, up to a bounce limit of
   50; a ray that reaches the limit is black.
2. Diffuse material scatters in a random direction around the surface normal and attenuates by its
   albedo.
3. Metal material reflects about the normal, blurred by a fuzz factor in 0..=1, and attenuates by
   its albedo. A reflection that points into the surface is absorbed.
4. Glass material refracts by its refractive index using Snell's law, reflects on total internal
   reflection, and chooses reflection by Schlick's approximation otherwise. It does not attenuate.
5. Each pixel averages a configurable number of samples (default 16), jittered inside the pixel,
   with gamma 2 correction on output.
6. All randomness comes from the seeded generator in `src/rng.rs`, seeded with a fixed value.

## Geometry

7. Every hit records whether the ray hit the front face, and the normal always points against the
   ray.
8. Every hit records texture coordinates `(u, v)` in 0..=1: spheres by latitude and longitude,
   planes by the hit point's position along two axes in the plane, modulo 1, and triangles by their
   barycentric coordinates.
9. The scene can hold infinite planes (a point and a normal) and triangles (three vertices).
10. Every object reports an axis-aligned bounding box, and the scene list tests a ray against an
    object's box before the object. An infinite plane has no box and is always tested.

## Output and command line

11. The image is written as PNG, with no external crate: one IDAT chunk holding zlib data made of
    stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with correct CRC-32 and Adler-32 checksums. PPM stays
    available.
12. The command line takes `--width`, `--height`, `--samples`, `--output <path>` and
    `--format png|ppm`. The defaults are 400 by 200, 16 samples, `render.png` and the format from the
    output file's extension. An unknown option or a bad value prints a usage line and exits with a
    non-zero status.
13. While rendering, a progress line on standard error shows the share of rows done.

## Quality

14. `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
